title: Ferrari Luce, First Electric Ferrari, Makes India Debut in New Delhi
excerpt: Ferrari unveiled the 1,050 hp Luce EV at Universo Ferrari in New Delhi, with CEO Benedetto Vigna calling India a source of talent and partnership, not just sales.
body:
• Ferrari unveiled the Luce, its first all-electric car, in India at the Universo Ferrari exhibition at Yashobhoomi in New Delhi, running October 17 to November 1, with public entry from October 19.
  • The Luce uses four electric motors making more than 1,050 hp, a 122 kWh battery and an 800V system, with 0-100 km/h in 2.5 seconds, a 310 km/h top speed and a claimed range above 530 km.
  • Global price is €550,000, about Rs 6.1 crore; Ferrari has announced no India price or launch date, so the Delhi showing is a debut, not the start of sales.
  • CEO Benedetto Vigna framed India as more than a market, calling it a source of talent, partnerships and opportunity.

Ferrari has brought its first all-electric car, the Luce, to India, unveiling it at the Universo Ferrari exhibition in New Delhi as chief executive Benedetto Vigna made the case for an electric Ferrari built around driver emotion rather than technology for its own sake. In an exclusive interview with the Hindustan Times, reported from the event, Vigna defended a top-down approach to breakthrough design.

"True innovation is never democratic"

— Benedetto Vigna, Chief Executive Officer, Ferrari

The fifth edition of Universo Ferrari runs at Yashobhoomi, the India International Convention and Expo Centre, from October 17 to November 1. Invited guests attend on October 17 and 18, and the exhibition opens to the public from October 19, according to coverage of the opening. Alongside the Luce, visitors can see the F80, the 12Cilindri Manuale, the 849 Testarossa, the Purosangue and the Amalfi Spider, plus the 499P Le Mans hypercar and the SF-26 Formula 1 car, Cartoq reported.

A Ferrari built electric from the start

Ferrari executives stressed that the Luce was not an existing model converted to batteries. "When we started the project five years ago, we had one clear objective in mind. We didn't want to develop a new electric vehicle. We wanted to develop a completely new Ferrari," Emanuele Carando, head of global product marketing, said at the exhibition. Andrea Binotti, head of the EV product line, called it "the first Ferrari born electric" and said the architecture uses 95% new components and more than 60 patents.

The numbers are conventional Ferrari territory. Four motors, one per wheel, produce a combined output reported at 1,050 hp and 990 Nm of torque. The battery sits beneath the floor, lowering the centre of gravity by 100 mm compared with a combustion-engine layout, and Ferrari claims 0-100 km/h in 2.5 seconds, 0-200 km/h in 6.8 seconds and a top speed of 310 km/h. Cartoq reported DC fast charging support of up to 350 kW and a claimed range of up to 530 km.

Design that has split opinion

The Luce was designed with LoveFrom, the collective co-founded by former Apple design chief Jony Ive. It is a four-door, five-seat car — a first for Ferrari — and at 5,026 mm long it is the largest Ferrari yet, Cartoq reported. The cabin mixes a 10-inch touchscreen and a 12.5-inch OLED instrument cluster with physical buttons and tactile controls, a deliberate move away from screen-only interiors. That styling has made the Luce the most debated car at the show, with enthusiasts divided over how far it departs from familiar Ferrari lines.

Why India, and what happens next

Vigna said India's energy and optimism matched Ferrari's own values. "We believe in India, and it's not something that is new," he said, recalling the brand's 2008 drive across India in two 612 Scagliettis covering about 13,000 km. He added that Ferrari sees India as a source of talent and partnerships as well as customers, and pointed to Avalon Lux becoming Ferrari's official Hypercar partner from January 2027.

For Indian buyers, the practical position is simple: there is no India price and no sales date yet. The global price of €550,000, about Rs 6.1 crore before Indian taxes and options, is the only figure Ferrari has put on the car. The Delhi exhibition is the place to see it in person until November 1.
